lenses.name: Population
lenses.description: Residents per km² of land. Each municipality's population (INE Padrón, 2025) is spread over its hexes in proportion to how much of the municipality each hex covers. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

lenses.name: Income
lenses.description: Mean net income per person of the municipalities in each hex, weighted by population (INE Atlas de Distribución de Renta de los Hogares, 2024: tax records matched to the Padrón). A mean per person, not the US map's median per household. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

lenses.name: Heritage
lenses.description: Bienes de Interés Cultural (Spain's highest heritage protection: monuments, sites, historic quarters) in each hex, as Wikidata locates them. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

lenses.name: Museums
lenses.description: Museums in each hex: the 2,517 museums, galleries, science centres and visitor centres in Spain that Wikidata locates. Hover a hex for their names. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

lenses.name: Ancient peoples
lenses.description: The ancient people whose Pleiades location is nearest to each hex (within 175 km): Vaccaei, Vascones, Cantabri, Ilergetes… and, in the south and east, the regions named after their peoples (Turdetania, Bastetania, Contestania). The borders are nearest-point territories drawn by this map: Pleiades gives each people a point, not a boundary.

lenses.name: Languages
lenses.description: Where each regional language is official, municipality by municipality, as the laws set it: co-official in all of Catalonia, the Balearic Islands, Galicia and the Basque Country; Aranese in Val d'Aran; Navarre's Basque-speaking and mixed zones (Ley Foral 18/1986); in the Valencian Community, the Spanish-speaking municipalities of Llei 4/1983 (Valencian is co-official there too); Asturian, protected but not co-official. Aragonese and Catalan in Aragon have no published list of municipalities yet, so Aragon shows Spanish only. Dialects (Andalusian, Canarian…) are not legal categories and are not mapped.
